files.delegate.sh:
#!/bin/sh
{
  printf 'argv0=%s\n' "${0##*/}"
  i=0
  for a in "$@"; do i=$((i + 1)); printf 'arg%d=[%s]\n' "$i" "$a"; done
  printf 'argc=%d\n' "$#"
  printf 'X=%s Y=%s\n' "${X-unset}" "${Y-unset}"
  fds=
  for n in 3 4 5 6 7 8 9; do
    if [ -e "/proc/$$/fd/$n" ]; then fds="$fds $n"; fi
  done
  printf 'open-fds=[%s]\n' "${fds# }"
  ign=0 blk=0
  while read -r k v; do
    case $k in SigIgn:) ign=$v ;; SigBlk:) blk=$v ;; esac
  done < /proc/$$/status
  printf 'usr1-ignored=%d term-ignored=%d blocked=%s\n' $(( (0x$ign >> 9) & 1 )) $(( (0x$ign >> 14) & 1 )) "$blk"
} > "rec.${REC_TAG:-run}"
case ${DELEGATE_ACTION-} in term) kill -TERM $$ ;; esac
exit "${DELEGATE_STATUS:-0}"

cases.purpose: Without the bash-os authority, doas runs BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL (or doas from PATH) with the original words unchanged, refreshes the exported environment at each call, closes inherited descriptors, resets signal dispositions and mask, propagates exit and signal statuses, and returns 127/126 when the delegate is missing or not executable; refused options and usage errors never start the delegate.
cases.oracle: doas front-end documentation ('Non-root callers use v2 authority when available, otherwise external doas'; usage synopsis), shell conventions for exec failure (127 not found, 126 not executable) and 128+N for a signal death, exported-variable semantics of bash (exported, not plain, variables reach children with their current values), and execve(2)/signal(7) inheritance rules. Delegate hygiene: descriptors above 2 closed (the caller holds 7 and 9 open), signal dispositions reset (the caller ignores SIGUSR1/SIGTERM) and an empty signal mask, observed by a POSIX sh recorder from /proc/self/status.
cases.comparison: Exact status, recorder observations (argv, environment, descriptors, signals) and whether the delegate ran.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t doas) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate doas builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
/usr/bin/chmod 755 delegate.sh bin/doas
unset BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL BASHSUDO_EXTERNAL X Y DELEGATE_STATUS DELEGATE_ACTION
trap '' USR1 TERM
exec 7< delegate.sh 9> fd9.tmp
run() {
  local tag=$1; shift
  export REC_TAG=$tag
  "$@" > "out.$tag" 2> "err.$tag"; local rc=$?
  printf '%s rc=%d delegate=%s diag=%s\n' "$tag" "$rc" "$([[ -e rec.$tag ]] && echo ran || echo not-run)" "$([[ -s err.$tag ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
  [[ -e rec.$tag ]] && /usr/bin/cat "rec.$tag"
  return 0
}
export BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL=./delegate.sh
export X=first; Y=local
run verbatim doas -u bob -- printf '%s' 'a b' '' $'line\nbreak'
X=second
run refresh doas id
export DELEGATE_STATUS=7; run status doas true; unset DELEGATE_STATUS
export DELEGATE_ACTION=term; run signal doas true; unset DELEGATE_ACTION
BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL=./missing.sh; run missing doas true
BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL=./plain.txt; run not-executable doas true
BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL=./delegate.sh
run unknown-flag doas -x true
run user-missing doas -u
run no-args doas
printf 'no-args-usage=%s\n' "$([[ -s out.no-args ]] && echo printed || echo none)"
unset BASHDOAS_EXTERNAL
PATH=$PWD/bin run default-path doas -n true
PATH=/empty run default-absent doas true
exec 7<&- 9>&-
trap - USR1 TERM
/usr/bin/rm -f rec.* out.* err.* fd9.tmp

cases.purpose: su resolves targets only from the private database (PHCLIB_PASSWD, else PASSWD_FILE): absent users and rows with non-numeric, reserved or empty ids or too few fields never select an account; an unreadable file and a directory report an unreadable database rather than a missing user; an eight-field row elsewhere in the file is parsed without harming the shell. No row is reachable, so nothing authenticates.
cases.oracle: passwd(5) seven-field rows with decimal uid/gid ((uid_t)-1 and (gid_t)-1 reserved), su(1) 'no such user' versus a database read failure (fopen/read errors such as EACCES and EISDIR are not absence), and the loadables' shared PHCLIB_PASSWD-then-PASSWD_FILE fixture selection.
cases.comparison: Exact status, empty stdout and diagnostic class (documented message keys) per lookup, and that the shell survives every lookup.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t su) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate su builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
export BASHPASSWD_KERNEL_SECRETS=0 PHCLIB_SHADOW=shadow.fixture
unset PASSWD_FILE
try() {
  local label=$1; shift
  su "$@" > out 2> err; local rc=$?
  local e; e=$(< err) c=other
  case $e in
    *"no such user: "*) c="no-such-user(${e##*no such user: })" ;;
    *"invalid user: "*) c="invalid-user" ;;
    *"cannot read passwd database"*) c="unreadable-db" ;;
    "") c=none ;;
  esac
  [[ -s out ]] && o=nonempty || o=empty
  printf '%s rc=%d stdout=%s diag=%s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$o" "$c"
}
export PHCLIB_PASSWD=passwd.fixture
for u in nosuch badchar uidmax gidmax emptygid sixf; do try "$u" "$u"; done
/usr/bin/cp passwd.fixture locked.fixture; /usr/bin/chmod 000 locked.fixture
PHCLIB_PASSWD=locked.fixture; try unreadable nosuch
/usr/bin/mkdir adir; PHCLIB_PASSWD=adir; try directory nosuch
: > empty.fixture; PHCLIB_PASSWD=empty.fixture; try empty-db nosuch
PHCLIB_PASSWD=; PASSWD_FILE=absent.fixture; export PASSWD_FILE; try fallback-variable nosuch
PHCLIB_PASSWD=passwd.fixture; try precedence nosuch
printf 'shell=alive\n'
/usr/bin/chmod 600 locked.fixture; /usr/bin/rm -rf out err locked.fixture adir empty.fixture
cases.stdout:
nosuch rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(nosuch)
badchar rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(badchar)
uidmax rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(uidmax)
gidmax rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(gidmax)
emptygid rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(emptygid)
sixf rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(sixf)
unreadable rc=1 stdout=empty diag=unreadable-db
directory rc=1 stdout=empty diag=unreadable-db
empty-db rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(nosuch)
fallback-variable rc=1 stdout=empty diag=unreadable-db
precedence rc=1 stdout=empty diag=no-such-user(nosuch)
shell=alive
